Q: Godot study, Developing games in godot using c# A:

To add to CJTheGoldfish: Maybe you should not use Godot in the first place. Maybe you should use something like MonoGame first. Not only is it native C# (which Godot is not), but it is also way more hands on and may give you a more broad understanding about game code which you can then apply in Godot (or any engine, really).

Q: Parse columnar values from a multi-line, formatted string A:

There is no need to split the input text, just capture the components from each line. Demo

preg_match_all(
    '#^(.+?)\h+([A-Z]{2})\h+(.+)#m',
    $codes,
    $matches
);
[, $language, $code, $family] = $matches;
var_dump($language, $code, $family);

^           #the m pattern modifier makes this symbol match the start of each line
(.+?)       #lazily match one or more characters as capture group 1
\h+         #match one or more horizontal spaces (e.g space or tabs)
([A-Z]{2})  #match two uppercase letters as capture group 2
\h+         #match one or more horizontal spaces (e.g space or tabs)
(.+)        #match the rest of the line as capture group 3

Q: 'list' object has no attribute 'json' A:

As @Kevin pointed out the each does not return a json, but a list. You can check it out on the pyrebase documentation.

Your code should probably look like this:

all_products = database.child("products").get()
for product in all_products.each():
    data.append(product.val()) # This works if your fields have the same names.

Edit

If you still need data as a JSON.

json_data = json.dumps(data)

Q: conversion of dataframe into Matrix in R A:

In R, a matrix is just a vector that is split up in certain places to form the rows and columns. Thus, all elements must be of the same type. In particular, if you have a data.frame with one column of numeric data, and one column of character data, you won't be able to convert it into a matrix. I don't know for sure, but it looks like column2 might be a character vector.

Note that I have no knowledge of the recommenderlab package.

An example:

df <- data.frame(col1 = c("A", "B"), col2 = 1:2, stringsAsFactors = F)

data.matrix(df)
#Warning message:
#In data.matrix(df) : NAs introduced by coercion

df
#     col1 col2
#[1,]   NA    1
#[2,]   NA    2

Q: VBA PowerPoint Search and Replace Returning Error on Uneditable WordArt A:

After a fair amount of research and experimentation I found the problem. It seems that individual objects in PowerPoint show themselves as unlocked even though are indeed locked and can not be edited.

To solve the problem, before editing, I simply lock and then immediately unlock the object.

Sub ProcessDocument(FilePath As String)
    Dim ppDoc As Object
    Dim ppApp As Object
    
    'MsgBox FilePath
    
    Set ppApp = GetObject(, "PowerPoint.Application")
    Set ppDoc = ppApp.Presentations.Open(FilePath)
    'Application.StatusBar = ppDoc
 
    Dim sld As Slide
    Dim shp As Shape
    
    For Each sld In ppDoc.Slides
        For Each shp In sld.Shapes
            If shp.HasTextFrame Then
                If shp.TextFrame.HasText Then
                    shp.Locked = True   'Lock the object
                    shp.Locked = False  'Unlock the object - clears a lock even if the lock  
                                        'was in place before the above lock
                    Set textLoc = shp.TextFrame.TextRange.Find("AAAA")
                    If Not (textLoc Is Nothing) Then
                        shp.TextFrame.TextRange.Text = Replace(shp.TextFrame.TextRange.Text, "AAAA", "----")
                    End If
                End If
            End If
        Next shp
     Next sld
    
    
    ' Save and close the document
    ppDoc.Save
    ppDoc.Close
End Sub
